An open-source, offline-first alternative to Garmin Connect. Not affiliated with Garmin. Licence: AGPL-3.0, Bluetooth sync ported from Gadgetbridge.
Read your watch with a USB cable or a folder, follow your heart rate live over Bluetooth, or pull your data from your Garmin account.
Read the watch with a USB cable

Plug the watch into the phone with its cable (USB-C, or with an OTG adapter). OpenConnect then copies the activities and the all-day data stored on the watch: steps, heart rate, stress, Body Battery, sleep, HRV and SpO2. It goes straight from the watch to this phone, not through Garmin or the internet.
No Garmin watch found on the USB port. Check the cable and that the watch is switched on, then search again.

Shows your heart rate live from a Garmin watch that broadcasts it, or from a chest strap. On the watch, look for Sensors & accessories, Wrist heart rate, Broadcast heart rate (the names differ per model).
Bluetooth permission is needed to find sensors.
The watch can sync over Bluetooth with OpenConnect itself (above), be read with a cable or from a folder, or send live heart rate. Data from Garmin\'s servers comes in on the Garmin screen.
Read a folder with watch files

Pick the GARMIN folder of the watch, a copy of it, or any folder with .fit files. Android\'s folder picker also lists a watch that is plugged in as a storage device. Files that were read before are skipped.
No .fit files were found in that folder.

Your watch talks to the Garmin Connect app on your phone over Bluetooth, and Garmin keeps your data in its cloud. OpenConnect reads your own data from there with a personal key that only you can create. There is no server of ours in between.
Make the key on Garmin\'s page (it is shown once), copy it and paste it below. OpenConnect keeps it encrypted on this phone and sends it only to Garmin.

Sync a Garmin watch over Bluetooth

Experimental. OpenConnect talks to the watch the way the Garmin Connect app does (the protocol Gadgetbridge worked out) and copies what is new: activities, steps, heart rate, stress, Body Battery, sleep and HRV. No cable, no Garmin account. The first time, Android pairs with the watch: put the watch in pairing mode (Settings, Connectivity, Phone, Pair phone) and confirm the code.
A watch paired with OpenConnect will in practice no longer sync with the Garmin Connect app. The files stay on the watch.
Pairing: confirm the code on the watch and the phone.
Could not connect to the watch: %1$s. If Garmin Connect is paired with this watch, use the Garmin account route instead.
The watch connected, but listed no files OpenConnect can read.
Pairing with the watch did not work. Put the watch in pairing mode (Settings, Connectivity, Phone, Pair phone) and try again.
Based on %1$d days with a reading.
Steady compared with the week before
Steps counted by your watch each day. Around 7,000 to 10,000 a day is linked with good health; the dashed line is 10,000.
Hours slept per night. Most adults do well on 7 to 9 hours; the dashed line is 8.
Your heart rate at rest. A lower number usually means better fitness; most adults sit between 50 and 80. A sudden rise can mean stress, illness or poor sleep.
Garmin\'s energy estimate, from 0 to 100. The line shows the highest value of each day: 75 or more means you charged well, under 50 means little recovery.
Heart rate variability overnight. It is personal: compare with your own normal, not with others. A drop of more than 10% below your average can mean you need rest.
Blood oxygen. 95 to 100% is normal; lower readings at altitude or from a loose watch are common, persistent values under 90% are worth asking a doctor about.
Breaths per minute. 12 to 20 at rest is normal; the value moves a little with fitness, illness and altitude.
Garmin\'s stress score from heart rate variability, 0 to 100: up to 25 is rest, 26 to 50 low, 51 to 75 medium, above 75 high.

A watch talks to one phone app at a time over Bluetooth. If Garmin Connect is your main app, keep it that way and let OpenConnect read the same data from your Garmin account (Garmin account screen) or from files. Use the Bluetooth sync here only when OpenConnect should be the watch\'s phone. Runs that arrive from more than one route are recognised and kept once.
Readiness is OpenConnect\'s own estimate. Sleep score, Body Battery and stress are the watch\'s numbers. No reading yet shows a dash.
OpenConnect\'s own 0 to 100 estimate from sleep, Body Battery, HRV, resting heart rate and stress, against your own normal. 70 or more means ready for a hard day, under 40 means take it easy.
The sleep score your watch gives each night, 0 to 100: 80 or more is good, 60 to 79 fair, below 60 poor. It weighs duration, deep and REM sleep and restlessness.
What you want to reach each week. The defaults follow common recommendations; set a goal to off with the minus button.
All goals are switched off. Turn them on in Settings.
This week %1$s points, your usual week %2$s
Clearly less than your recent norm. Fine for recovery; if it was not planned, an easy session gets you going again.
In line with the last four weeks. This is the range where fitness builds with the least risk.
More than usual. Fine for a short block, but plan an easier week after it.
A big jump over what your body is used to. This is the usual time for niggles and illness: back off a little.
OpenConnect\'s own estimate: minutes times an effort weight from your heart rate, this week against your 4-week average. Not Garmin\'s Training Load, not medical advice.
